text:
morgan: CI canary publish is failing on `canary/experimental-2026` after my Dockerfile reorder (moved COPY before apt installs). I can push the image locally to artifactory but the CI push to `registry.internal` errors out during blob upload.

morgan: here are the tail of the CI logs:
```
PUT /v2/org/app/blobs/uploads/xxxxxxxx?digest=sha256:abcdef
-> 412 Precondition Failed
upload: chunk 3/8 failed: unexpected EOF
error: write tcp 10.0.0.7:443: write: connection reset by peer
Docker-Distribution-Api-Version: registry/2.0
```

alex: do we know if this is a buildx-only problem or also with docker build + docker push? can you share the `buildx` command you used in CI?

morgan: CI runs `docker buildx build --push --tag registry.internal/org/app:canary-2026 --platform linux/amd64,linux/arm64 .` and uses cache-from pointing at previous canary. locally i did `buildx` and push to a personal repo and it worked.

tess: :eyes: that pattern looks like we've seen when the proxy or registry gateway resets chunked uploads mid-stream. Could be intermittent upstream (lb/proxy) or a client not sending content-length properly. Any chance the reordered Dockerfile changed layer size distribution and triggered chunking differences?

jamie: I'd try two quick checks:
- rerun CI with `DOCKER_BUILDKIT=0` (classic push path) to see if buildx chunking is the culprit
- rerun with `--no-cache` to avoid cache-from causing resumed uploads

morgan: ok i'll queue a rerun with both flags.

morgan: when rerun started: `2890011199` (kicked off manual rerun)

infra-bot: registry alert: connection reset spikes from proxy-02 during 2026 canary window (2890011185-2890011202). Correlating logs: proxy-02 returned 502 to upstream stream during multipart upload.

tess: sounds like a transient proxy flake. alex, can you grep proxy logs for `upload-id=xxxxxxxx` and see if we have a truncated TCP connection? if proxy is dropping connections we need infra oncall to look at proxy-02.

alex: will check, pinging @eng-sre.

jamie: if infra can confirm proxy reset, we should retry CI job and consider adding a retry wrapper around `docker buildx build --push` in our CI to handle transient upload resets. Also open a short postmortem if it recurs.

morgan: rerun finished: still failing but different symptom:
```
POST /v2/org/app/blobs/uploads/ -> 409 Conflict: upload session not found
```

tess: that suggests resumed upload sessions not surviving; either cache-from is causing resume attempts against stale upload-ids or proxy is rewriting/losing state. two asks:
1) morgan: can you try `--push` but with a fresh tag (no cache-from) to ensure a clean upload path
2) alex/eng-sre: grep registry for `upload session not found` and proxy timestamps around 2890011190-2890011250

morgan: queued clean build with `--no-cache` and fresh tag `canary-2026-clean` (started 2890011230)

alex: quick note from logs: proxy-02 hit a socket full condition, kernel dropped backlog; engineering infra has a mitigation in progress (scaling proxy pool). tagging @eng-sre to confirm rollout.

infra-bot: eng-sre acknowledged, creating incident INC-28900 for proxy-02 socket backlog.

jamie: long-term we should ensure CI buildx has N retries for upload chunks; short-term, retry the job after infra scales the proxy pool. morgan, hold off on more changes until proxy fix lands.

morgan: thanks — holding. opened a tiny PR to add retry wrapper and a CI flag to opt into it: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/7722 (WIP) :slightly_smiling_face:

alex: :thumbsup: if this ends up being proxy capacity, we should mark the canary as flaky and avoid automatic rollouts until resolved.

morgan: noted. i'll link CI run and follow up once infra confirms proxy fix. thanks all.
